sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Marysville, Ohio?
sections.html:
You can list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or sell to a cash buyer who takes it in its current condition. Whichever route you pick, the paperwork ends at the same two Union County desks: the auditor, who processes the transfer, and the recorder, who files the deed.

The best route depends on the shape of the house and how soon you need to be done. A listing reaches the widest pool of buyers but usually brings inspection requests, showings and a wait. A cash sale trades some of that reach for a faster, simpler close.

  • Agent listing: the most exposure, plus repair negotiations and a commission to plan for.
  • For sale by owner: no listing commission, but you handle pricing, showings, the contract and the state disclosure form on your own.
  • Cash buyer: an offer for the house as it stands, with the closing date often set around your schedule.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Marysville housing?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 30,190 residents in Marysville for July 1, 2025, compared with 25,571 counted in April 2020. Its QuickFacts page shows that gain at 17.9 percent measured from the 2020 estimates base.

For 2020-2024, the same page lists a median owner-occupied home value of $300,800 and an owner-occupied rate of 67.5 percent. Median gross rent is $1,223, median household income is $92,619, and the city has 10,163 households averaging 2.46 people. Median monthly owner costs run $1,851 with a mortgage and $681 without one.

These are citywide medians. Your own house sells for what the buyer in front of you will pay, so ask for a written price review of recent sales on your street before you decide anything.

sections.h2: Why do buyers look at Marysville?
sections.html:
Marysville is the Union County seat, about 27 miles northwest of Columbus, and its large employers give buyers a reason to live close by. Scotts Miracle-Gro, founded here in 1868, keeps its headquarters in the city, and Honda's Marysville Auto Plant sits roughly six miles to the northwest, where it has built the Accord since 1982.

Nestle runs a Product Technology Center on the west side, and Univenture and a Parker Hannifin plant are also based in town. U.S. Route 33 is a four-lane highway through Marysville that links to Interstate 75 in one direction and the I-270 outerbelt in the other.

The city earned the nickname the Shaded City in 1888 for its tree-lined streets. Today it has more than 300 acres of parks, with trails along Mill Creek, and the Union County Fair runs from late July into early August.

sections.h2: Which school district serves a Marysville house?
sections.html:
Almost all of Marysville belongs to the Marysville Exempted Village School District, and a few parcels extend into Fairbanks Local. Because the district sets part of the tax bill, confirm it for your parcel instead of assuming.

The Union County auditor's GIS map has a school district layer for this purpose. The auditor's FAQ adds a detail that matters on boundary lots: when a district line passes through a house, the district where the master bedroom sits is the one that taxes the whole house.

To see your rates, find the parcel on the auditor's site and open the "Where your taxes go" link. The Total Effective Rate column is the rate for that property.

sections.h2: What must a Marysville seller disclose under Ohio law?
sections.html:
An Ohio owner selling a property with one to four dwelling units must complete the state's residential property disclosure form and give buyers a signed, dated copy (Ohio Revised Code 5302.30). The form asks about water supply, the sewer or septic system, the roof, foundation, walls and floors, hazardous materials such as lead paint, asbestos and radon, and any known material defects.

Several transfers are excluded from the requirement:

  • Sales ordered by a court, and transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate, guardianship or trust.
  • Transfers to a spouse or to relatives in the direct line of the seller.
  • A sale by someone who inherited the house and has not lived there in the past year.
  • A sale to a buyer who has already lived in the house as a residence for a year or more.

If a buyer receives the form after already signing a contract, the buyer may rescind in writing within three business days of getting it. That right ends no later than 30 days after the offer was accepted or at closing, whichever is earlier.

sections.h2: What happens at the Union County auditor and recorder when a Marysville house sells?
sections.html:
The grantor signs the deed and acknowledges it before a notary or another official named in Ohio Revised Code 5301.01. The deed then goes to the Union County Auditor, whose office sits at 233 W. Sixth St. in Marysville, before it reaches the recorder.

At the auditor, the buyer or the buyer's representative files a statement of value (DTE 100) or, for an exempt transfer, a statement of the reason (DTE 100EX). The seller pays the conveyance fee. Ask the auditor for the current rate before closing, since the county can add its own levy on top of the state portion.

The recorder will accept a conveyance by mail only when the auditor's conveyance stamp is already on it. Per the posted schedule, a deed costs $39.00 for the first two pages and $8.00 for each page after that. Copies cost $2.00 a page.

sections.h2: When are Union County complaints and exemption notices due?
sections.html:
A Board of Revision complaint on a Union County parcel must reach the auditor between January 1 and March 31 of the year after the tax year in question. The table lists that and the other dates Union County prints for owners.

Union County items for Marysville owners
ItemWhat the county prints
Board of Revision complaintReceived after January 1 and on or before March 31
Appeal of a Board of Revision decisionWithin 30 days of the decision letter, to the Board of Tax Appeals or Common Pleas Court
Homestead exemption, change in statusNotify the auditor by the first Monday in June
Refund after a value reductionDecisions are held 30 days, then adjustments follow in about sixty days
Deed recording fee$39.00 first two pages, $8.00 each added page

Source: Union County Auditor FAQ and Union County Recorder fee schedule.

  • The 2.5 percent rollback applies to owner-occupied homes and one property per owner, and owners have to apply for it.
  • A change of more than $50,000 in market value (or $17,500 assessed) triggers notice to the school board.
  • A recent sale supports a complaint when you file the closing statement, purchase contract and deed.

sections.h2: Do Marysville improvements need permits before a sale?
sections.html:
Yes, most exterior additions in Marysville need a city zoning permit, and some also need a building permit from the Union County Building Department. The city's permit page names decks, fences, swimming pools, sheds, garages and room additions, plus public sidewalks and driveway approaches, which must be built by a contractor licensed with the city.

Before you list, ask the city zoning office whether anything on your lot was built without a permit. A buyer's inspector will notice an old deck or shed, and a cash buyer will factor it into the offer instead of asking you to fix it first.

sections.h2: What should a Marysville landlord know before selling?
sections.html:
Ohio law requires the owner of residential rental property to file contact information with the county auditor and update it within 60 days of a change (Ohio Revised Code 5323.02). When a rental parcel changes hands, the auditor's endorsement on the deed reminds the new owner of that filing.

If tenants live in the house, ask the buyer how they plan to handle the lease. A buyer who wants the house empty will want a different timeline than one who keeps the tenants.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Marysville owner?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when speed or condition matters more than squeezing out the top price. Typical situations include:

  • An inherited house that nobody plans to live in.
  • Deferred repairs on a roof, furnace or foundation.
  • A tenant situation that makes showings hard.
  • A job move that needs a fixed closing date.

Compare any offer with what a listing would net after repairs, commission and carrying costs, and read the contract for who pays closing charges.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Marysville house without making repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Ohio does not require repairs before a sale, though you must disclose known problems on the state form. Cash buyers purchase as-is, while a buyer with a mortgage may ask for repairs after an inspection.

faqs.q: Who pays the conveyance fee on a Marysville sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 puts the conveyance fee, and any county transfer tax, on the grantor, and the auditor endorses the deed to show it was paid.

faqs.q: When can I challenge my Marysville property value?
faqs.a: The Union County window runs from January 1 through March 31 for the current tax year. You file a notarized Board of Revision complaint with the auditor by email, fax or mail, and only the current tax year can be contested.

faqs.q: Does an inherited Marysville house need the disclosure form?
faqs.a: Often it does not. Ohio excludes transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate, and also a sale by an heir who inherited the house and has not lived there in the past year.

faqs.q: How do I find the tax rate for a Marysville parcel?
faqs.a: Search the parcel on the Union County auditor's website and open "Where your taxes go." The Total Effective Rate column gives the rate, and the Treasurer's rate summary lists every tax district.
